answer: A plot auction sells one grove's plots each epoch, one per key. A plot takes an 80-credit bond and a key-signed cipher bid; the registrar posts plot, bid, and key to a mirror ledger, bond refunded after a season. Bidding closes at zenith: the first plot clears at 30 credits, each later plot costs 8 more, so the kth costs 30+8(k-1) and the 1000th costs 8022; 1000 fakes pay 4,026,000 in bids plus 80,000 locked, so total cost grows quadratically. A rented cipher fails: the registrar matches bid key to claimant key and burns the bond on mismatch. An honest agent pays 30 once, bond refunded.
